instruction: Apply italic formatting to titles in slides 3, 5, and 6.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires applying italic formatting to titles in slides 3, 5, and 6. Evaluator extracts title italic property from these slides and verifies it is True.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 1.0 = All 3 titles are italic, 0.67 = 2 titles are italic, 0.33 = 1 title is italic, 0.0 = No titles are italic
metadata.verification: Verified by analyzing actual PowerPoint file structure: file contains 6 slides with titles in Gloria Hallelujah and Poppins fonts. Target slides identified based on slide indices.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies italic formatting on the right slides (0-based indices 2, 4, 5 = human slides 3, 5, 6)
Postconfig appropriately saves the file before verification
Metric scoring logic correctly implements partial credit as specified in scoring_breakdown
Title detection uses heuristic (largest font size) which may be unreliable - actual title placeholders would be more robust
Getter only checks first run of title text - won't detect mixed formatting within a title
If a slide has no detectable title, it's silently skipped which could skew scoring
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Use shape.has_title or check placeholder type to identify title shapes more reliably instead of relying on largest font size heuristic
Check all runs in the title text and verify they all have italic formatting, or check the paragraph-level formatting if applicable
Handle missing titles explicitly - either fail the verification for that slide or document the assumption that all target slides must have titles
